records.claim: Oil markets weighed recovering Middle Eastern supply against new disruption risks; Saudi Arabia reported East-West Pipeline flows of 5.8 million barrels per day.
records.observation: The Saudi bypass is carrying substantial volumes and reinforces the existing route-adaptation trajectory.
records.assessment: PERSISTENT / STRENGTHENING, NOT A NEW DELTA.

records.claim: The IEA governing board was due to discuss implementation of the G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude stocks; detailed volumes and participation remained unresolved.
records.observation: This is implementation work on the October 2 policy delta, not a fresh commitment.

records.claim: A Gulf of Mexico storm was forecast to become a hurricane and threaten offshore areas producing about 15% of US crude and 5% of US natural gas.
records.observation: The risk is material but remained prospective; no confirmed physical flow loss was established in the evidence reviewed.
records.assessment: DEVELOPING / FORECAST RISK, NOT PHYSICAL DELTA.

records.claim: Atlantic LNG freight rates fell sharply from March peaks as 55 new LNG vessels were delivered in the first seven months of 2026 and shorter Atlantic-basin voyages increased vessel availability.
records.observation: Transport capacity has expanded faster than current shipping demand, reducing freight scarcity despite strong European LNG demand.
records.assessment: STRUCTURAL CONTEXT / CAPACITY EXPANSION; insufficient evidence for a same-day state transition.
